entities.summary:
Joseph Volotsky, a prominent Russian theologian and early proponent of tsarist autocracy, played a pivotal role in shaping the Russian Orthodox Church's stance on monastic landownership. Born Ivan Sanin, he led the party defending monastic landownership in the dispute with the non-possessors, ultimately securing a favorable outcome for the church. Volotsky's memory is celebrated on September 9 and October 18, and his patronage is over businessmen.

As a leading figure in the dispute, Volotsky collaborated with other notable theologians of his time, including Patriarch Filaret I of Moscow, to establish a unified stance on the issue. This collaboration resulted in the adoption of a new church constitution that solidified the church's authority over monastic land. The dispute also led to the establishment of the Synod of Moscow, a governing body that would play a crucial role in shaping the Russian Orthodox Church's policies for centuries to come.

The consequences of Volotsky's actions were far-reaching, as they helped to establish the Russian Orthodox Church as a dominant force in Russian society. His legacy can be seen in the many monasteries and churches that were built during this period, as well as the continued emphasis on the importance of monastic landownership in the Russian Orthodox tradition.

Volotsky's significance can be seen in his role as a key figure in the development of the Russian Orthodox Church's doctrine, particularly with regards to its stance on monastic landownership. His actions helped to shape the church's policies and establish its authority over monastic land, a legacy that continues to be felt today.

The impact of Volotsky's actions can be seen in the many Russian monarchs who would go on to rule the country, including Peter the Great and Catherine the Great. These rulers were heavily influenced by the Russian Orthodox Church's stance on monastic landownership and went on to implement policies that reflected this influence.
